questions.questionText: What does the sigmoid function do in logistic regression?
options: It removes outliers from the training data
It squashes the linear combination z into a probability between 0 and 1
It computes the gradient for training
It converts categorical features into numbers
questions.correctAnswer: It squashes the linear combination z into a probability between 0 and 1
questions.explanation: z = w·x + b can be any real number; sigmoid maps it smoothly onto (0, 1) so it can be interpreted as a probability.

questions.questionText: Why does logistic regression use log loss instead of mean squared error?
options: Log loss is simpler to compute
Log loss penalizes confident-but-wrong predictions much more sharply, which suits probability estimates
There's no real difference between them
questions.correctAnswer: Log loss penalizes confident-but-wrong predictions much more sharply, which suits probability estimates
questions.explanation: A confidently wrong prediction (e.g. predicting 0.99 for a true negative) incurs a very large log loss, giving the optimizer a strong signal to fix egregious mistakes.

questions.questionText: The decision boundary that separates two classes in plain logistic regression is:
options: A random curve fit by the model
questions.explanation: Since the boundary is defined by z = 0, and z is a linear combination of the features, the boundary is inherently linear — the same geometric limitation as linear regression.
